exposure: Longitudinal incision in one uterine horn (CS horn)
Short incision at the tip of the contralateral horn (control horn)
outcome: Number of vessels in scar tissue
Oestrogen receptor presence in scar tissue
Progesterone receptor presence in scar tissue
Resistance to rupture after balloon inflation
cohort: Eighteen pregnant primiparous female rabbits who underwent an experimental caesarean section.
finding: The scarred area of the uterus after caesarean section was significantly thinner, more fibrous, contained fewer vessels and hormone receptors, and was more prone to rupture compared to non-scarred or control areas, with individual factors influencing healing quality.
followup_time: Approximately 42 days (14 days after initial CS plus 28 days of subsequent gestation) after the experimental caesarean section.
gest_age: 28 days (at the time of the experimental caesarean section)
